correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs every needed step. Conservation gives 0<=i<=N. The positive Neumann resolvent fixes constants, hence 0<=b<=N. On this reachable interval, h(b)<=b^p<=max(1,N^(p-1))b for every p>=1, with no condition relating p and q. Combining this with the exact Neumann identity integral b=integral i and the source's finite space-time infected mass gives finite space-time incidence. Fubini and the exact susceptible formula then give positive limiting susceptibility. Pointwise and L1 extinction and the remaining monotone limits use only conservation, bounded derivative, and dominated convergence. No finite experiment is used as proof.

value.rationale: The restriction excludes the entire superlinear-unsaturated-tail regime p>q+1 from the source's long-time theorem even though the model itself never reaches arbitrarily large infectiousness. Removing it closes the theorem across the full exponent range p>=1,q>=1 stated in the model. The mechanism is structurally meaningful: a conserved population cap, transmitted through a positive elliptic resolvent, makes the global tail growth of the incidence irrelevant to extinction and residual susceptibility.
